html:
The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the Monastery of the Caves, is a great Orthodox monastery on the hills above the Dnieper in Kyiv. It was founded in 1051 by the monk Anthony, who had lived on Mount Athos, and grew around the caves he and his followers dug into the hillside.

Under Anthony's follower Theodosius it became an organised community with a rule taken from the Stoudios monastery in Constantinople. It was the leading monastery of Kievan Rus' and a centre of learning. The monk Nestor, long named as the author of the Primary Chronicle, the main history of early Rus', lived there. Monks were buried in the caves, where their bodies still lie and draw pilgrims.

The monastery was wrecked in the Mongol invasion of 1240 and rebuilt several times. In the 17th century it ran one of the most important printing houses of Eastern Europe. With Saint Sophia Cathedral, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
